chunks: Yahyā ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:
Whoever sells a slave, and the slave has wealth, then the wealth belongs to the seller unless the buyer stipulates otherwise. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, commanded that.

key_terms.الْبَائِعِ: the seller, who retains the wealth by default
key_terms.الْمُبْتَاعُ: the buyer, who may stipulate inclusion of the wealth
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, whose command establishes the ruling
key_terms.عَبْدًا: a slave being sold in the transaction
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth owned by the slave

ai.seo_question: When a slave is sold in Islamic law, does the slave’s wealth go to the seller or the buyer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sale of a slave who possesses wealth. The default rule is that the slave’s property remains with the seller unless the buyer explicitly makes it a condition of the sale, and the ruling is attributed to the command of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
